title: Slab-built decorative cake stand
subtitle: A two-tier air-dry clay cake stand built from round slabs and a central column , decorative use only
excerpt: Two circular clay slab tiers are assembled on a central clay column to create a display cake stand. The piece is decorative rather than food-safe , air-dry clay is porous and cannot be guaranteed food-safe after painting. The construction teaches slab building, column construction, and balancing a stacked piece during drying.
sourceNotes: Decorative cake stand in air-dry clay derived from first principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: A flat, even sheet of clay rolled to a consistent thickness
The method of roughening and applying diluted clay before joining two clay pieces
The stage at which clay is stiff enough to support additional pieces without collapsing

content.text: Air-dry clay is porous and cannot be food-safe certified. This cake stand is for display purposes , for candles, dried flowers, paper decorations, or craft supplies. Do not place edible food directly on the surface.
This two-tier stand is built in stages: base disc first, then the column, then the top disc. Each piece is brought to
leather-hard
before assembly. The
score-and-slip
joins must be made carefully , the column carries the weight of the upper tier and any wobble will be visible.

items.name: Two round card or plate templates: 200 mm and 140 mm diameter

content.text: Make the tier discs
Roll a clay
slab
to 8 mm thickness. Cut a 200 mm circle (the lower tier) and a 140 mm circle (the upper tier) using the card templates and fettling knife.
Smooth both discs and allow to dry to leather-hard on a flat surface.
Make the column and base foot

Roll a solid clay cylinder 30 mm in diameter and 80 mm tall. This is the central column. Ensure it is truly vertical , a leaning column will tip the top tier. A quick way to check: stand it on the work surface and view from all angles.
Roll a small foot disc 60 mm in diameter and 8 mm thick. This sits beneath the column and adds stability. Smooth and allow all three pieces to reach leather-hard.
Assemble the stand
Score-and-slip the top of the foot disc and the bottom of the column. Press together firmly, centring the column on the foot. Blend the join around the column base.
Turn the 200 mm base disc upside down. Score-and-slip the underside centre and the top of the foot assembly. Press together. Allow to dry until firm enough to flip upright without the column moving.
Score-and-slip the top of the column and the underside centre of the 140 mm top disc. Press together and allow to dry in place.
Dry, paint, and seal
Allow the assembled stand to dry fully to bone-dry. Check all joins are solid before painting.
Paint with two coats of acrylic paint. Apply two coats of PVA varnish to all surfaces.

items.problem: Column is not vertical , stand leans
items.solution: Correct this before the assembly dries fully. Dampen the join at the base, adjust the column, and prop with a wadded piece of cloth while drying.

items.problem: Top tier disc cracks at the join
items.solution: Both surfaces need to be at matching leather-hard dampness for score-and-slip to bond. If the top disc was too dry, the join will be weak. Reattach with PVA adhesive at bone-dry stage.
